transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. Um, I hope I'm explaining this right, but... I guess I'm here because I've been having a little trouble with my daily routine. It's probably nothing too serious, I just... well, I've been losing a lot of time—sometimes hours, actually—just rechecking things. 

It's mostly just everyday stuff. Like my door locks, or things for my engineering work, like file dimensions and revision notes... even just my dressing supplies in the morning. I just get this feeling that I'm not, um, allowed to move on to the next task until I've gone through the exact same routine enough times. I basically have to keep doing it until the anxiety finally drops. I know that probably sounds really irrational, and I'm sorry if it's a bit strange. Does that make sense? Is that the kind of thing you usually help people with?
Do you feel like you have to perform these routines or checks, or is it something you can stop doing if you want to?

I mean... I'd really like to say that I can just stop whenever I want. I try to, I really do. I'll tell myself, 'Okay, you looked at the revision notes, you checked the locks, it's fine.' But... if I try to just walk away or skip the rest of the routine, the anxiety just spikes. 

It's like I was mentioning before, I just don't feel *allowed* to move on to the next thing. I basically have to stay there and keep repeating the checks until that awful feeling finally drops. That's how I end up losing those hours I mentioned. I really wish I could just snap out of it and be normal about it, and I'm sorry if that makes me sound completely unhinged. Am I... am I explaining that clearly enough for you?
Do you feel like you have to think specific thoughts or repeat certain words or phrases in your head as part of these routines?

Um, no, I don't think I really do that. I don't repeat specific words or phrases in my head, at least not that I've noticed. I hope that's an okay answer, I don't want to be unhelpful. 

It's really just... well, I know I'm sort of repeating myself, and I'm really sorry to sound like a broken record, but it's mostly just the physical act of checking. Like I mentioned before, it's just going through the actual routine with the door locks or the file dimensions at work. I don't really have a specific thought in my head other than just waiting for that anxiety to drop so I feel allowed to move on to the next thing. 

Is that... does that answer your question okay? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Are these rituals and repeated checks affecting your relationships or work performance?

Well... I try really hard not to let it inconvenience anyone else. I really want to be a good employee, you know? But, um... I guess, if I'm being completely honest, my project deadlines have started slipping a little bit. 

It's not that I'm slacking off, I promise. I just... I end up staying late at the office, just trying to get comfortable enough with everything to actually submit the work. I hope that doesn't make me sound incompetent. I really do care about my job. 

And as for outside of work... well, I used to go to these paddleboarding meetups, and I liked to work out, but I've kind of stopped making it to those. The routines just sort of... eat up all the time I used to keep for myself. I feel really guilty about letting my friends down when I don't show up. 

I hope I'm not sounding like a complete mess. I'm really trying my best to keep it all together. Is it... is it normal for things to spill over into my schedule like that? Am I giving you the kind of information you need?
Do you experience any intrusive or unwanted thoughts that disturb you or cause you distress?

Um... well, I guess... I mean, I really don't want to sound like I'm completely losing my grip or anything. But... yeah, I do get these thoughts sometimes that just won't leave me alone. 

Like, even after I *know* I’ve cleaned a wound area perfectly well, or... or at work, after I've reviewed a CAD file over and over. I'll just get this thought cutting in that I missed one tiny little thing. And my brain just insists that this one tiny oversight is going to turn into a horrible infection, or... or a design mistake that actually hurts someone. 

I try so hard to just reason it away and tell myself it's fine, but I just can't. It just sticks there until I do something about it. I know that probably sounds incredibly irrational, and I'm really sorry if it's weird... is that the kind of thing you meant? I just hope I'm not sounding too crazy to you.
Do you feel like these intrusive thoughts are coming from your own mind or do they feel like they're imposed on you from the outside?

Um, no, they definitely feel like they're coming from me. Like, it's my own brain doing it, not... not voices or anything from the outside. I know it's just my own head making me worry about these things. 

I really hope that doesn't make it sound worse, like I'm doing it to myself on purpose. I'm definitely not trying to think these things, it's just... my own thoughts getting kind of stuck, I guess? 

I just want to be clear that I know it's all in my own head. Does that make sense? I hope that's a normal way to experience it.
How much distress do these intrusive thoughts cause you?

Um... well, I mean, it's not like I'm completely falling apart or anything. I really don't want you to think I'm incapable of handling my life, or that I'm just sitting around crying. I try really hard to stay positive and just push through it! 

But, I guess... if I'm being totally honest, it is pretty frustrating. It just makes me feel really tense and sort of... trapped, I guess? At least until I can go back and re-check the file or, you know, do whatever my brain is telling me to do. 

It's not unbearable, I promise. I manage it okay most days. It's just really uncomfortable when it gets stuck in my head like that. 

I hope I'm not making a bigger deal out of this than I should be. I know other people probably deal with way worse things. Does that answer your question okay? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right kind of information.
Do you feel like you're checking things to prevent something bad from happening?

Um, yeah, I guess that's a big part of it. I mean, I really try not to let it take over, and I don't want to sound like I'm completely obsessed or anything... but, well, the truth is, I do end up spending a lot of time checking things. 

Like, I'll check my dressing supplies to make sure they're perfectly clean, or I'll check the door locks, or at work, I'll go over the file dimensions and revision notes again and again. It's just... I guess I feel like I'm not really allowed to move on to the next thing until I've gone through that routine enough times. Like, I just have to keep doing it until the anxiety finally drops and I feel like it's safe to stop. 

I'm actually losing hours to it sometimes, which is... kind of embarrassing to admit. I really hope that doesn't make me sound totally incompetent at my job or anything. I'm still getting my work done! It just takes me a bit longer sometimes. 

Is that the kind of thing you were asking about? I just want to make sure I'm explaining it right and not making it sound weirder than it is.
Do you feel like your checking behaviors are intended to prevent harm to yourself or others?

Um, no... not really. I mean, I definitely don't want you to think I'm worried about, like, hurting anyone or myself! It's nothing dangerous like that, I promise. I'm actually a really careful guy, I'd never want to cause any harm. 

It's not really about preventing a specific disaster or someone getting injured. It's more just... well, like I was saying before, it's just this really strong, nagging feeling that something isn't quite right yet. Like the file isn't perfectly formatted or the door isn't properly secured, and I just can't relax until it feels right. But I'm not sitting there picturing people getting hurt or anything terrible like that. 

I really hope that makes sense? I'm not sure if that's the typical way people experience this, and I hope it doesn't make my answers seem inconsistent. I just want to be totally honest with you so you have what you need. Did I explain that okay?
Do you feel like you have to follow specific rules or arrangements when you're doing your daily tasks or routines?

Um, no, not really? I mean, I hope it's okay if my answer to that is no. I definitely don't want to mess up your evaluation or seem like I'm leaving anything out. But I don't really have strict rules or, you know, specific ways I absolutely *have* to arrange my desk or my apartment. 

I mean, I like things to be organized—just with my engineering work, it helps to be a little tidy—but I'm not super rigid about it, I promise! I'm pretty flexible with most things. I don't have a special sequence for how I get dressed or make my coffee or anything like that. It's really just the checking stuff that I mentioned before. 

Does that make sense? I hope that's a helpful answer. I just want to make sure I'm doing a good job explaining things for you and giving you what you need.
Do you feel like you have to think about or mentally replay certain events or images as part of your daily routines?

Um, no, I don't think so. I really hope it's okay that I keep saying no to some of these questions! I don't want you to think I'm holding anything back or being uncooperative, I promise. I'm just trying to be as honest as possible. 

But, um, no, I don't really have any specific events or images that I feel like I have to mentally replay. My thoughts are usually pretty grounded in whatever I'm working on, especially with my engineering projects. I definitely don't get stuck repeating things in my head like that. It's really just the physical checking stuff I mentioned earlier. 

I hope that's a helpful answer? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right kind of information for your evaluation. Am I doing okay with all of this?
Do you feel like you have to think about or mentally replay certain numbers, words, or phrases as part of your daily routines?

Um, no... no, I don't think I do that either. I feel a little bad, like I'm just shooting down all your questions! I really, really hope I'm not frustrating you or making your job harder. I just want to give you the exact truth so you can do your assessment properly.

But, yeah, I don't really get stuck on numbers or specific words or anything like that. My mind is usually just focused on my work, you know, the actual calculations or whatever I'm doing for my job. I don't have, like, a special phrase I have to repeat in my head to feel okay. It's really just the checking things physically, like I was saying before. 

I hope it's okay that I don't have that symptom? I just want to make sure I'm being a good patient and giving you what you need to figure all this out. Does that make sense?
Have you had to make significant changes to your daily life or work habits to accommodate these checking behaviors and intrusive thoughts?

Um, well... I guess maybe a little bit? I mean, I really try not to let it affect things too much, I promise. I try to keep everything under control so I'm not, you know, being a burden or letting anyone down at work. 

But, um... I guess lately, some of my project deadlines have started slipping just a tiny bit. It's just because I end up staying late, trying to make sure everything is perfectly checked and I feel comfortable enough to actually submit the work. I really want to do a good job, you know? So I just take a little extra time. 

And, um, outside of work... I guess I haven't been going to my paddleboarding meetups or my regular workouts as much recently. The checking stuff just kind of eats up the time I used to keep for myself. But I'm sure it's just a phase, and I'll get back on track soon! 

I really hope that doesn't make me sound like a terrible employee or anything. I'm still working really hard! Is it okay that I'm struggling with this a little bit? I just want to be honest with you so you can help me.
Have you avoided any activities or places because of your checking behaviors or intrusive thoughts?

Um, no, I don't think I've really avoided any specific places or activities... at least, not intentionally! I mean, like I said, I've missed a few of my paddleboarding things lately, but that's just because I run out of time, not because I'm actually avoiding the water or the people or anything like that. 

I really try to push through and do normal things, you know? I don't want to be one of those people who just hides away. I try my best to keep up with everything. So, no, I wouldn't say I'm actively avoiding anywhere. 

I hope that's the right kind of answer? I just want to make sure I'm giving you an accurate picture of what's going on. Am I doing okay explaining all this?
Have you experienced any significant difficulties in your social relationships due to your checking behaviors or intrusive thoughts?

Um, no, not really. I mean, I think my relationships are pretty okay. I really try to be a good friend and, you know, show up for people when they need me. 

I guess maybe I've been a little less available lately just because I'm so busy with work and... and staying late to double-check things, like I mentioned. So maybe I haven't been as social as I usually am. But I don't think it's caused any, like, big fights or major problems with anyone. I always try to text people back and let them know I'm just caught up with stuff. 

I really hope my friends don't think I'm ignoring them. I try to make sure they know I still care. But, yeah, no major difficulties or anything like that. Does that make sense? I hope I'm not making it sound like I'm a bad friend or anything.
Do you feel like your checking behaviors are intended to prevent something bad or harmful from happening to yourself or others?

Um, well... maybe a little bit? I mean, I don't want to sound like I think the world is going to end or anything crazy like that. I know realistically that checking a lock won't stop everything bad in the world. 

But... I guess, yeah, I do kind of feel like I have to do it to keep things safe. It's actually sort of the main reason I decided to come see you. I'm just... I'm losing hours every day to rechecking things. Like, um, my dressing supplies in the morning, the door locks before I leave, and then at work it's the file dimensions and my revision notes. 

I just... I don't feel allowed to move on to the next thing until I've gone through the whole routine enough times. It's like my anxiety just stays so high until I do it just right, and then it finally drops and I can breathe again. I just want to make sure everything is okay and no one gets hurt or messed up because of me. 

I really hope that doesn't sound too strange or obsessive. I just want to be a responsible person, you know? Is it normal to feel like you have to do things a certain way to make the anxiety go away? I hope I'm explaining this right.
Do you feel like you have to perform any mental rituals, such as counting or saying certain words to yourself, as part of your daily routines?

Um, no, not really mental rituals, I don't think. I don't sit there counting in my head or repeating words or anything like that. I try to keep my thoughts pretty normal, you know? 

Like I was saying before, the main thing that brings me in is just that I'm losing so many hours to physically rechecking things. You know, like the dressing supplies, the door locks, and then at work with the file dimensions and my revision notes. It's more about doing those physical routines enough times until the anxiety finally drops and I feel allowed to move on. 

But I don't do the mental counting stuff. I really try not to let it get to that point. I hope that's okay? I just want to make sure I'm answering exactly what you're asking. Does that make sense for what you're looking for?
Have your checking behaviors and intrusive thoughts significantly impacted your ability to function in daily life?

Um, well... I really try my best not to let it get in the way of things. I always want to be a good employee and, you know, stay on top of everything. But... I guess if I'm being completely honest, maybe it has impacted things a little bit? 

Like, um, at work—I'm an engineer—some of my project deadlines have started slipping just a tiny bit. Not because I'm not working hard! I'm actually staying late almost every day. It's just... I spend that extra time trying to get comfortable enough with everything to actually submit the work. I just want to make sure it's exactly right so my team doesn't get let down. 

And then outside of work, I guess I’ve sort of stopped making it to my paddleboarding meetups... and I haven't really been doing my normal workouts either. It's just that the routines kind of eat up all the time I used to keep for myself. 

I really hope that doesn't make me sound lazy or irresponsible. I'm honestly trying so hard to keep it all together and be productive. Does that answer what you were asking? I hope I'm giving you the right kind of information.
